Week 5 · Listening to Conversations in Detail

Overheard at the Gate

At an airport gate, you hear conversations all around you: plans changing, people agreeing, people politely saying no. This week you'll listen closely to conversations like the ones on the DET: who wants what, what they think, and how they feel. Then you'll try a full Interactive Listening set. You choose your own level. Go at your own pace. There's no grade, and finishing all the steps counts as attending this week.

~45 min total Choose your level 🎧 Headphones recommended One DET-style set A short recording
Interactive ListeningListen and Complete, Listen and Respond, Summarize
Tone & opinionsHear agreeing, disagreeing, suggesting and saying no
SpeakingRetell a conversation in your own words
STOP 01~2 min

Choose Your Cabin

Pick the level that feels right today. Your choice changes the conversations, how many times you can play each clip, and your summary time. Every cabin counts the same for attendance, and you can switch any time.

Sound check: play this before you start. It doesn't count as a play.

STOP 02~3 min

Pre-flight Briefing

DET FORMAT · INTERACTIVE LISTENING

On the DET, Interactive Listening puts you inside a conversation with a classmate or a professor. Each set has three parts in a fixed order. Match each part to what it asks you to do: tap a name, then tap its description. A tip appears for each correct match.

STOP 03~6 min

Tone Check

DET SKILL · TONE AND OPINIONS

People often don't say yes or no directly. Read the situation, listen to one line, and decide how the speaker feels. After you answer, you'll see the signal phrase that tells you, plus more phrases like it.

TIPListen for small signal words: but, though, well…, maybe, I'm afraid. One small word can change the meaning of the whole sentence.
All signal phrases (a list to keep)
STOP 04~5 min

Next Transmission

DET PRACTICE · LISTEN AND RESPOND

On the DET, you are one of the speakers. Listen to the other person, then choose what you would say next. Wrong answers are wrong in a few typical ways, and the feedback names each one.

TIPThe best reply answers the last thing you heard, fits the situation, and uses the right tone. A professor needs a polite reply. A classmate can be casual, but not rude.
STOP 05~6 min

Flight Log

DET SKILL · FOLLOWING A WHOLE CONVERSATION

Listen to a whole conversation between two people. You can type quick notes while you listen. Then fill in the flight log and press Check.

TIPDon't write full sentences. Write key words for the problem, what each person thinks, and the decision. These are also what a good summary needs.
STOP 06~10 min

Full Flight

DET PRACTICE · FULL INTERACTIVE LISTENING SET

Now put it all together: one complete set in the same order as the DET. You'll hear a new situation, then take part in the conversation, then write a summary.

STOP 07~5 min

Radio Check

BONUS · SPEAKING ABOUT WHAT YOU HEARD

Retell your Full Flight conversation to a friend who wasn't there. Record it on Vocaroo (free, no account needed) and paste the link below so I can listen and send you feedback.

  1. Open vocaroo.com in a new tab. It works on a computer or a phone.
  2. Take 30 seconds to plan using the cue card. Don't write a script. Just a few key words for each part.
  3. Press the red record button (allow the microphone if asked) and talk. Use your own words.
  4. Press stop, then Save & Upload. Copy the link it gives you (it looks like voca.ro/… or vocaroo.com/…).
  5. Paste the link here:

Nervous about recording? That's normal. Only I will hear it, and my feedback will focus on one or two helpful things, not every mistake.

STOP 08~2 min

Landing Card

This is Week 5's primary assignment. Add one listening tip you will use on test day, then copy your summary and paste it into the Week 5 assignment in Classroom. That counts as attending this week.

Copied! Now paste it into Classroom.
✓ LANDED — SEE YOU IN CLASSROOM

Duty-Free Shop: Free Listening Tools

Free sites with short conversations at your level. Listening a little every day helps more than listening a lot once a week. Pick one or two you like.

Official DET Practice: try this week's question types

On Duolingo's free practice page, try the question types below. They use the same skills you practiced today: following a conversation, choosing good replies, and summarizing.

Open the practice page → Quick practice test
MAIN FOCUS · Stops 02–06Interactive ListeningListen and Complete, then Listen and Respond (5–6 turns), then Summarize the Conversation in 75 seconds.
STRATEGY · Stop 04Choosing repliesCross out replies that don't fit the situation, don't match what was said, or use the wrong tone.
STRATEGY · Stops 05–06Summarize the ConversationSituation → main points → ending, in full sentences. Your Flight Log notes are a good plan.
ALSO TRYListen and TypeType the sentence you hear. The Week 3 skill, and great practice for catching small words.
